change_note: Pre-registered rule set 1.0.0: monthly index autopilot and lump sum as the core plan; Five Leaders (three forms) as the testable satellite; v1, random baskets and all-21 as yardsticks; fixed numbers (10 bps, seed 20261005, 17 tries, 182 paper days); planned checks marked not computed.
trader:
We are savers first. Once a month, on the first trading day after pay arrives, a standing order buys a broad index fund (our core), whatever the news. We never pause it and never sell the core in a crash. Money we already have, such as a bonus (a windfall), goes in all at once. Today that is the only real action.

A small stock pot (at most a tenth of our savings, 2% per stock) opens only after a rule passes two main checks: first on past prices, then on a written paper record (no real money) kept at least half a year. The pot is a separate holding; only its own parked index money is traded, on review days. The rule we will test is Five Leaders. Each month it ranks our 21 companies by their rise over the past year, ignoring the latest month, and holds up to five, one per sector. A newcomer must be above a rising 200-day average price and not over 8% above its 50-day average. A holding leaves if it falls below the 200-day average or is no longer picked. Empty slots wait in the index fund. Past-price tests reset holdings to equal each month; in real life names start equal, are never topped up, and winners may drift.

We will NOT: buy on tips, headlines or AI picks; add money to a falling stock; use stop orders or trade stocks between review days; borrow or use options; change a rule after a loss; grow the pot to chase +20% a year. Real money follows a stock rule only if every money condition in the acceptance text is met, including beating random picks and the index fund after costs. Nothing here promises any return. If no rule earns a place, the pot stays in the index fund.

rules.name: Monthly autopilot: one automatic purchase a month
rules.plain: Every payday a standing order buys the index fund with that month's savings, whatever prices did. Dividends are reinvested. Never paused. It starts now, with no paper period. It is the plan every other savings plan is compared with.
rules.definition: Live: on the first trading day after pay arrives, put all of that month's savings into the core index fund at the next close. No price condition, no pause in a fall, no extra at a high. Reinvest dividends. Test today: stream mode, one unit of cash arrives each week and everything on hand is bought every 4 weeks (the monthly stand-in; about 12 to 13 orders a year). Cash waiting earns the T-bill fund return (zero before that fund existed). Fill at the next close. Start dates every 4 weeks; horizons 52, 104 and 156 weeks. It is the baseline row, so it gets the verdict word 'baseline', never better or worse.

params.name: every_weeks (live and test)
params.why: Monthly matches a monthly pay date. The library only describes monthly purchases (S-020.P03, S-050.P01) and never compares cadences, so E01 tests it. Evidence: mixed. A test 'week' is 5 trading days: 4 weeks is about 12.6 buys a year against 12 live.

params.name: price condition
params.why: Never stopping mattered more than timing in the library (S-050.P01). A trend-based pause is not registered here.

params.name: dividends
params.why: The test uses adjusted prices, so payouts count as reinvested. Live, the broker must reinvest them (S-050.P03).

params.name: units
params.value: fractional if offered, else whole units
params.why: Whole shares came within a fraction of a point of fractional ones (S-050.P02). Not a reason to wait.

params.name: trading cost in the test
params.why: The savings test charges no trading cost. It prints orders a year and the fixed fee per order at which two plans tie. Compare that with the broker's real fee.

params.name: waiting cash
params.value: earns T-bill fund return, zero before it existed
params.why: Zero is pessimistic for cash in the early years. Reported as is.

params.name: horizons and start step
params.why: Fixed before any run. A week is 5 trading days. With about 2,500 to 2,600 daily bars the 52-week row has about 8 to 9 independent windows, 104 weeks 4, 156 weeks 2 to 3: probably only the 52-week row can give a verdict, and under about 2,300 bars none can.

params.name: amount
params.value: set by the owner; not stored in the repo
params.why: The test uses one unit a week. The real amount is private and changes only at the yearly rule review.

rules.why_included: It is the core plan and the baseline for all savings arms. It is the easiest rule for a household to keep and it removes the urge to time the market. Support is consistent but thin: one book (S-020.P03) and one video-series note on a single start at a high (S-050.P01). Rated mixed.
rules.adopt_if: Adopted from day one, with no paper period; the order starts now and does not wait for the signed plan. A savings arm replaces it only through rule_change_protocol at the yearly review, and only on the engine verdict 'better' (8+ independent windows) or, for the quarterly arm, when the broker's real fee per order is above its printed break-even fee.
rules.reject_if: No history test can reject it; its own verdict is 'baseline'. It changes only at the yearly review, through rule_change_protocol: if pay stops arriving monthly, or the broker's fee per order is above the quarterly arm's printed break-even fee (fewer orders then win).

rules.definition: Report-only arm. Stream mode: one unit of cash arrives each week and everything on hand is bought every 1 week (about 50 orders a year). Cash waits the least. Cash waiting earns the T-bill fund return. Fill at the next close, no gate. Compared by start date with the 4-week baseline over horizons of 52, 104 and 156 weeks (starts every 4 weeks): median yearly-return gap, share of starts ahead, orders a year, and the break-even fixed fee per order.

rules.name: Cash windfall goes in all at once
rules.plain: Money we already have beyond the emergency reserve (a bonus, a sale, a starting balance) goes into the index fund in one purchase. Only money that has not arrived yet is spread over time. The owner may choose otherwise, in writing.
rules.definition: A windfall is cash on hand beyond the written emergency reserve and beyond the regular monthly savings. It is bought in the core fund in one order at the next close. Test today: windfall mode. 100 units are in hand on day one and all are invested at once (spread of 1 week). Horizons 52, 104 and 156 weeks, start dates every 4 weeks. It is the windfall baseline row, so its verdict word is 'baseline'. No trading cost is charged in this test.

params.name: spread_weeks
params.why: S-007.P03 says a lump sum beat holding cash for a better entry. It does not test equal weekly staging; that is what the 26 and 52 week arms measure. The default is an inference plus the library's warning against waiting. Evidence: mixed.

params.name: what counts as a windfall
params.value: cash beyond the emergency reserve and the monthly savings
params.why: Money needed soon is not investable. The reserve size is private and not stored in the repo.

params.name: highs
params.why: Highs cluster (S-007.P01) and a high alone is no bearish signal (S-007.P04). Library evidence, not tested here.

params.name: waiting for a dip
params.why: People who wait for a dip tend to buy back higher (S-007.P02).

params.name: what the test prints
params.value: median multiple, yearly return, worst moment below money put in
params.why: Printed for each arm and compared by start date. The lump-sum row is the yardstick for the staged arms.

params.name: owner choice
params.value: staging is allowed if written down before the windfall exists
params.why: It is recorded as a preference with its printed cost, never as a test result.

rules.why_included: It covers money already in hand, which the monthly plan does not. It has one parameter. Support is S-007.P03 (a lump sum beat holding cash for a better entry, from one video) and S-007.P01/P04 on highs; it does not test staging. Rated mixed: dry spells exist and the data here is one rising period.
rules.adopt_if: Adopted from day one as the default for any windfall. A staged arm replaces it only on the engine verdict 'better' (8+ independent windows, gain of 50 basis points a year or more, ahead in 80% or more of starts) and through rule_change_protocol.
rules.reject_if: No history test can reject it; its verdict is 'baseline'. The owner may still pick staging in writing before the money is invested, for comfort. That is a stated preference, not a finding that staging wins.

rules.name: Cash windfall spread over 26 weeks (comparison only)
rules.plain: Put a windfall in the index fund in equal weekly parts over half a year instead of all at once. Report-only. It may feel safer. The test shows what that comfort gave up or gained in the past. It is weakly supported.
rules.definition: Report-only arm. The windfall is split into 26 equal parts. One part is bought at each weekly step for 26 weeks, each at the next close. The part not yet bought earns the T-bill fund return. Compared by start date with the lump sum over horizons of 52, 104 and 156 weeks (starts every 4 weeks): median multiple gap, median yearly-return gap, share of starts ahead, and the worst moment below the money put in. No trading cost is charged.

rules.name: Five Leaders: main version, with the 200-day trend check
rules.plain: Each month, rank our 21 companies by their rise over the past year (skipping the latest month); hold up to 5, one per sector. A newcomer must be above a rising 200-day average price. A holding goes if it is below that average or out of the top 10, unless it still qualifies as a newcomer and a slot is free.
rules.definition: Everything in the basic version (same ranking, top-10 retention, stretch veto, 1 per sector, 5 slots reset to equal at each review, 10 bps, next-close fills, split- and dividend-adjusted closes). Added, at the monthly review only: a NEW name needs its close above its 200-day average AND that average higher than 21 trading days earlier. A HELD name is kept only while it ranks in the top 10 and its close is above its 200-day average. A released name can be picked again as a new name if it passes the new-name tests and a slot is free after the better-ranked names; otherwise the slot goes to the next allowed name, else the index fund. Never checked daily; no stop orders between reviews. This is the 'Five Leaders' satellite.

params.name: long average
params.why: S-050.P04 gives 200 days for mega-caps and indexes but 150 for individual growth stocks. The 21 names mix both, so 200 is one fixed choice, not tuned. 150, 160 and 250 days are planned neighbour checks (E06), not computed yet. Evidence weak.

params.name: rising line (entry only)
params.value: average today above its value 21 trading days ago
params.why: S-050.P05 says the average must be flat or rising and gives no number. We require it strictly higher than 21 trading days ago (21 = one review step), stricter than flat. House choice, not tuned. Evidence weak.

params.name: exit check
params.value: review day only; close below the 200-day average
params.why: The library source says exit on any daily close below the long average (S-050.P07) but offers no backtest (S-050.P11). We deliberately deviate: review day only, a house convention (no trading between reviews), so a break can be held up to a month. S-046.P04 is about added stops. Evidence weak.

params.name: proceeds
params.value: wait in the core index fund
params.why: A false exit then costs relative return, not market exposure.

params.name: everything else
params.why: Slots, keep buffer, stretch veto, sector cap are the same; their evidence is weak or mixed.

params.name: tries
params.why: Adjusted p = p times 17, the same bar as the basic version.

params.name: provenance of the numbers
params.value: 200 days and 8% echo the site's setup checks
params.why: The site's setup checks, whose real-price base rates were published before this registry, use similar numbers. No result of this rule had been seen, but the settings are not clean of that history.

rules.why_included: This is the satellite the household wants to run. The 200-day line is the written test of whether avoiding downtrends helps. The source for it offers no backtest, so the evidence is weak.
rules.adopt_if: Verdict passes_history: adjusted p <= 0.05 (17 tries), 60th percentile or better in both halves, deepest drop within 15 pts of the core, turnover <= 200%. The paired with-and-without 200-day test is not computed yet. Money needs every condition in the acceptance text (a first screen only: passes_history opens no money).
rules.reject_if: Verdict rejected (under the 50th percentile of the random baskets). If only the no-trend-check version (five_leaders_m1) passes_history, the owner reads the two rows side by side and writes the choice down; there is no paired test yet. Turnover above 200% or a drop 15+ pts worse than the core blocks passes_history.

rules.name: Five Leaders: basic version, no trend check
rules.plain: Each month, rank our 21 companies by their rise over the past year, skipping the latest month. Hold up to 5, one per sector, and skip any that jumped too far above their recent trend. A holding stays while it is in the top 10 of the 21. No trend check.
rules.definition: Decided at the close of the first trading day of each month, using closes up to that day (split- and dividend-adjusted); filled at the next close; 10 bps per unit of weight traded. Only names with 253 trading days of unbroken history are eligible. Rank: close 21 trading days ago divided by close 252 days ago (same order as excess return over any benchmark). A held name keeps priority while it ranks in the top 10 of the eligible names; a released name can be picked again like a new name if a slot is free. A new name must not be stretched: its close is under 8% above its 50-day average. At most 1 name per sector. 5 slots, each 1/5 of the stock pot, reset to equal at every review. No correlation cap, no 200-day line, no daily stops. Unfilled slots stay in the index fund.

params.name: strength measure
params.value: close 21 days ago / close 252 days ago
params.why: The library favours relative strength over about 6 months (S-040.P01) and 12-month index returns (S-030.P01). S-030.P03 says apply momentum to broad indexes, NOT single names, so a 21-name stock version goes beyond the library. The 12-1 form and the skip are house choices, untested. Evidence weak.

params.name: slots and sizing
params.value: 5 slots, 1/5 each, reset to equal at every review
params.why: House goal of 4 to 5 names. The engine cannot do 'drift, no top-ups' yet, so backtests reset monthly. Sizing is held fixed across rules (S-043.P03).

params.name: keep buffer
params.value: held name stays while rank is 10 or better
params.why: About half of 21 names, so a name leaves on lost strength, not a wobble. Meant to cut turnover (S-021.P05, S-026.P05). Not tuned. Evidence weak.

params.name: stretch veto
params.value: new names only; close under 8% above the 50-day
params.why: House 'never chase' rule. The library has no tested number: S-050.P08 calls 15 to 20% above the long average extended (a scale-out rule, untested) and S-010.P01 is about an index, not a stock. S-050.P04 distrusts 50-day averages as signals. Evidence weak.

params.name: sector cap
params.why: Names in one sector move together (S-035.P04, S-014.P03). The library gives no number. Evidence weak. No correlation cap, because provider correlations are doubted.

params.name: review timing
params.value: first trading day of each month
params.why: Once a month, so people look less often (S-032.P02). Fixed, not tuned.

params.name: tries
params.why: Needs adjusted p <= 0.05: at most 4 of 2000 random baskets at or above it (about the 99.8th percentile).

params.name: provenance of the numbers
params.value: 8% and the 50-day line echo the site's setup checks
params.why: The site's setup checks, whose real-price base rates were published before this registry, use similar numbers. No result of this rule had been seen, but the settings are not clean of that history.

rules.why_included: The plain version of the idea: buy the strongest names, one per sector, do not chase. It is the base that the 200-day line is added to, so we can see what that line changes.
rules.adopt_if: Verdict passes_history: adjusted p <= 0.05 against the random baskets (17 tries), 60th percentile or better in both halves, deepest drop within 15 pts of the core, turnover <= 200%. Money needs every condition in the acceptance text (a first screen only: passes_history opens no money).
rules.reject_if: Verdict rejected: beats under the 50th percentile of the random baskets. Turnover above 200% a year or a deepest drop more than 15 pts worse than the core stops it reading passes_history, and it cannot carry money.

rules.name: Five Leaders: reviewed every three months
rules.plain: The same as Five Leaders, but we only look in January, April, July and October. The aim is fewer trades and less temptation to tinker. We do not know yet whether it helps or hurts.
rules.definition: The same as Five Leaders with the 200-day line (ranking, top-10 retention, stretch veto, 1 per sector, 5 equal slots, 200-day entry and exit checks, 10 bps, next-close fills), but decided at the close of the first trading day of January, April, July and October, and once on the first test day (whatever its month), using closes up to that day. Between reviews nothing is bought or sold. Names still need 253 trading days of unbroken history. Unfilled slots stay in the index fund. The random baskets are decided on the same days.

params.name: review months
params.why: One look per quarter. Fixed, not tuned. Evidence untested.

params.name: everything else
params.why: Only the review calendar differs, so any gap comes from timing alone.

params.name: hoped benefit
params.why: Trading less is the best-documented help to owners (S-021.P05, S-026.P05), but whether a slower review helps this rule is untested. It may also react too late.

params.name: tries
params.why: Adjusted p = p times 17, the same bar as monthly.

rules.why_included: Fewer looks may mean fewer trades and more patience for two non-experts. Costing it as a counted arm shows what a slower calendar gives up.
rules.adopt_if: Verdict passes_history like the others. If monthly Five Leaders also passes, quarterly is chosen only by the E05 rule: percentile within 10 points of monthly and turnover at most 60% of monthly. If only quarterly passes, it is used. Paper only, no money.
rules.reject_if: Verdict rejected (under the 50th percentile of its own random baskets), or it fails the E05 comparison with the monthly version: then monthly stays.

rules.name: Rule v1: the stock rule the site already runs
rules.plain: The stock rule the site already runs. It holds up to 5 companies that pass at least 3 of 4 setup checks and are not stretched, and resets them to equal size every month. Used for comparison only: its history was seen before we wrote the rules down.
rules.definition: As in docs/methodology.md 'Portfolio rule v1'. At the close of the first trading day of each month: keep a held name while it passes at least 2 of the 4 setup checks (close above its 50-day above its 200-day average; 3-month and 6-month strength against QQQ; not stretched, meaning under 8% above its 50-day average). Add names that pass at least 3 checks and are not stretched. Rank by checks passed, then 6-month strength. At most 2 per sector; no pair with 1-year correlation above 0.85. 5 slots, equal weight, reset to equal every month. Empty slots stay in the core fund. No stops. Fills at the next close, 10 bps per unit traded.

params.name: checks to enter / to keep
params.why: As the site runs it today (config/settings.json). Not tuned for this registry. Evidence weak.

params.name: stretch limit
params.why: House 'never chase' value, for new names only. The library has no tested number; S-010.P01 only says stretched markets tend to pause.

params.name: sector and correlation caps
params.value: max 2 per sector; no pair above 0.85
params.why: As implemented, kept so the reference stays exact. The Five Leaders rules use 1 per sector and no correlation cap.

params.name: benchmark
params.why: As implemented. Pointing it at the core fund would make a v2 with a new record.

params.name: sizing
params.why: As implemented. Recorded turnover is 419.6% a year counting buys and sells (data/market/longrun.json: same-close fills, shorter window), about 210% of the pot replaced; the engine prints its own figure on the full history.

params.name: highest verdict allowed
params.why: Its history was viewed before registration. The engine enforces this: a passes_history reading is printed as candidate, with the reason.

params.name: tries
params.value: counts inside the one global N of 17
params.why: Every adjusted p-value uses the same 17, so this rule gets no cheaper bar than the others.

rules.why_included: Every new rule must be compared with the rule already running. Its history and its setup-check gate were seen before this registry, so they count as spent tries, not as clean evidence.
rules.adopt_if: Never from history alone: capped at candidate, and a candidate has no plan role and no money. It can move up only by the candidate route: at least 24 months of registry forward record (data/portfolio/paper_rules.json, next-close fills), forward percentile 80 or more, 100% on-time orders, and the turnover and drop limits still met. The older paper.json uses same-close fills and does not count.
rules.reject_if: Engine verdict rejected (under the 50th percentile). passes_history is also blocked while turnover is above 200% of the pot replaced a year; site records put v1 near 210% on that basis (419.6% counting buys and sells), so the engine's own figure decides. A lower-turnover version would be a v2 with a new record.

rules.name: Equal slots at purchase, no top-ups, winners drift
rules.plain: Each company we buy gets one equal slot, about 2% of savings. We never add to a winner or a loser. A winner may grow, but if one name passes a quarter of the pot we trim it back to a fifth at the next review. By hand; no test covers it yet.
rules.definition: Household practice: when a name is bought it gets 1/5 of the stock pot, paid for from the pot's own parked index units (or the proceeds of the name it replaces). After that it is never topped up and never averaged down, and its weight drifts. A single name that grows past 25% of the pot is trimmed back to 20% at a review. Backtests do NOT do this: the engine resets every slot to equal at each review, which sells winners, adds to laggards and counts that trading as turnover. The drift arm (E04) is reserved and needs engine work, so this rule is process_only until then and no result checks it.

params.name: slots
params.value: 5 slots; 1/5 of the pot each (about 2% of savings at a 10% pot)
params.why: House goal. A total loss of one slot costs about 2% of savings, the ceiling in S-045.P01 and S-040.P03 (most traders stay at 1% or less, S-035.P01), though those assume a stop. About 15 names capture diversification (S-028.P02); 5 is concentrated. Evidence mixed.

params.name: top-ups
params.why: Adding to a fallen name is not information (S-047.P02). S-036.P02 allows averaging down only when unlevered, capped and on a business thesis; we never do it.

params.name: drift
params.why: Cap the downside, leave the upside open (S-035.P03). Not tested here.

params.name: trim
params.value: above 25% of the pot, back to 20%, at a review
params.why: A name grown too large is a valid reason to sell (S-024.P05). The 25% line is a convention. S-043.P05 warns that trimming winners is reverse sizing, allowed only if it is the one way you can hold. Not run in any test.

params.name: backtest sizing
params.why: What the engine can do today. Sizing alone can change results a lot (S-043.P03), so the gap between reset and drift is unmeasured.

rules.why_included: Monthly resets conflict with the household's wish to hold winners and never add to losers. Writing the practice down now keeps it fixed before any result is seen, and flags that the tests do not match it yet.
rules.adopt_if: Adopted now as a written habit for any funded stock pot. E04 judges it once the engine can run drift with matching random baskets; until then no data can reject it.
rules.reject_if: E04 is the single source: drift is dropped only if its deepest drop is more than 5 points worse than the reset version AND it saves less than 40% of the trading, at 10 bps, in both halves. Until then only the rule-change protocol changes it.

rules.name: Stock pot size: at most 10% of savings, filled once
rules.plain: The stock pot is at most 10% of our investable savings (the owner confirms), so each of 5 slots is about 2%. It is filled once, never topped up, and never grown to chase the +20% goal. If it grows past 15%, it is trimmed back.
rules.definition: During the paper record no money moves. If ever funded, the owner decides the size, at most 10% of investable savings (index fund plus pot, not the emergency reserve), and writes the source down once: new money or a windfall, else a one-time sale of core index units (may be taxable). After that the pot is its own holding. A name is bought from the pot's parked index units or the proceeds of the name it replaces; nothing is bought from salary or the core. Salary keeps going 100% to the core. Annual band: above 15% of the total, sell the same share of every held name back to 10% and buy the core; below 5%, do nothing. Needs the household-account test (E11), not built, so process_only.

params.name: size limit
params.value: at most 10% of investable savings (owner confirms); 2% per slot
params.why: docs/household.md proposes 10%. The library says speculative money should be 'a few percent', separate and capped (S-020.P04, S-022.P01), so 10% is above it: our convention, and the owner decides. Evidence weak.

params.name: trim band
params.value: above 15% of the total, back to 10%
params.why: A house convention reusing the 5-point stock/bond band of S-022.P04. Not tested. Evidence weak.

params.name: check
params.why: Rebalance about once a year and look less often (S-021.P03, S-032.P02).

params.name: top-up
params.why: Speculation sits in a separate account that is never topped up (S-022.P01). A growing pot never chases the +20% goal.

params.name: review of the whole idea
params.value: after 36 months funded, if behind the core by money-weighted return, close the pot
params.why: A convention, not evidence. S-003.P02 warns a strategy winning 3 years in 5 is often behind for stretches, so 36 months can fire in an ordinary losing stretch (about 1 in 3 in a coin model). Reopening is a rule change. 60 months is an option.

params.name: who decides
params.why: The registry sets the ceiling; size and timing are the owner's call.

rules.why_included: It caps the household's worst case at about a tenth of savings for almost no effort. It is a safety limit, not a return rule, so hindsight has little to flatter.
rules.adopt_if: Adopted now as the size limit for any funded satellite. Once the household-account test (E11) exists it is judged by how often the 15% band fires, the share traded and the cost, never by return. The owner confirms the 10% before any money moves.
rules.reject_if: No price data can reject it. It changes only through the rule-change protocol: the owner picks a different size, or real costs make even one trim a year not worth it. Never changed while the index fund or the pot is 20% or more below its high.

rules.name: Drawdown playbook: a drop triggers a check, never a trade
rules.plain: If the index fund or the stock pot is 10, 20 or 30% below its high at a monthly review, we write it down and run a short check. We never buy or sell because of the drop. The monthly purchase continues, and an emergency reserve outside the plan means a fall never forces a sale.
rules.definition: Read by hand at each monthly review, from month-end values in USD against the highest month-end value so far; no code computes it today. Index fund down 10%: write it down. Down 20%: also re-read the written pre-commitment. Down 30%: also confirm the emergency reserve is at its written size. Stock pot down 10%: write it down. Down 20%: also check the last 3 reviews followed the rules. Down 30%: also re-read the pre-commitment. At every level: contributions continue unchanged, the rules run unchanged, no rule change is made, nothing is bought or sold because of the depth. Before any money moves, both adults sign that they can watch each fall 50% without selling; if not, make the pot smaller now, never during a fall.

params.name: levels
params.why: Read at month ends only, on the review calendar, so we look less often (S-032.P02). The levels are conventions.

params.name: action
params.value: none: same contribution, no sales, no extra buys
params.why: Starting at a high still did well; never stopping matters most (S-050.P01). Selling after falls costs the gains (S-020.P03). S-031.P05 concerns high valuations and advises trimming exposure somewhat; we do not follow that part, only its 'never exit wholesale'.

params.name: emergency reserve
params.value: outside the plan; size written by the owner
params.why: Being forced to sell is the real risk in a deep fall (S-034.P03). The size is the owner's call.

params.name: tolerance
params.value: signed in advance: able to watch a 50% fall without selling
params.why: If you cannot, you should not own that much (S-028.P03). Decide before, not during.

params.name: evidence note
params.why: Principles on holding through a fall (S-028.P03, S-020.P03) are in tension with others that cut risk in drawdowns (S-046.P02, S-040.P03). Nothing was tested on this household's data; the no-action stance is our choice.

rules.why_included: The most likely way the plan fails is a person selling in a crash. Writing the response down in calm times, as a check rather than a trade, is the cheapest protection.
rules.adopt_if: Adopted now as a written habit. Checked by the journal: an entry at every level reached, and zero trades caused by drawdown depth. Nothing in the engine scores it.
rules.reject_if: No price data can reject it. It changes only through the rule-change protocol, and never while the index fund or the pot is 20% or more below its high. If either adult cannot sign the 50% line, the pot is made smaller; the playbook stays.

rules.name: One signed plan, no overrides, one calendar
rules.plain: Before any stock money we sign a one-page plan. After that we never trade on a tip, a headline, the AI, a hunch, a fall or a rise. We decide only on review day and place orders within a few days. We write every decision down.
rules.definition: A private one-page plan, never in this public repo, signed before any stock money and re-signed yearly. It names the rules, the pot size (owner's choice, at most 10% of savings, 2% a slot), and who places and checks orders. Decide only on review day. Orders are exactly the rule's list plus the two written trims, placed within 5 trading days. Write a dated note before each buy and write down every decision. We will NOT: buy on tips, headlines or the AI's picks; buy a stock far above its recent average; add money to a falling stock; use stop orders or trade between review days; borrow or use options; pause the monthly index purchase or sell the index fund in a crash; change a rule after a loss or outside the yearly review; grow the stock pot to chase +20%.

params.name: review day
params.value: first US trading day of the month (quarter for the quarterly arm)
params.why: Matches the engine's decision day for the stock rules. The index-fund purchase follows pay day, not this date; the monthly checklist only confirms the order went through.

params.name: order window
params.value: within 5 trading days, next day preferred
params.why: The engine tests fills at the next close only (lag 1). A 5-day check is planned, not computed yet.

params.name: banned triggers
params.value: tips, videos, headlines, AI picks, analyst calls, a price fall or rise
params.why: Trade only your own analysis; tips and others' opinions ended careers (S-035.P05). Never add because a price fell (S-047.P02). Never sell a sound business only because its price fell, nor buy it only because it rose (S-022.P06). Orders from a registered rule's list are the exception.

params.name: half-drop sentence
params.value: We can watch the core and the stock pot each fall 50% without selling
params.why: Decide before the drawdown, not during it (S-028.P03).

params.name: departure limit
params.value: 1 override or late order resets the record; a 2nd in 12 months sells the pot
params.why: Our convention. A second departure in any rolling 12 months sells the pot into the index fund at the next review; the pot then returns to the paper stage with its record kept. A third to a half of people given identical written rules still failed on execution (S-046.P05).

params.name: re-funding
params.why: Our convention. It borrows the 20-sample floor of S-044.P02, which is about judging an edge, not regaining trust. Count only reviews where every listed order was placed in the window.

params.name: succession
params.value: 2 missed reviews: sell the pot into the index fund
params.why: A plan that needs one person will not last years. Our convention; untested.

params.name: monthly index purchase
params.why: A fixed purchase removes the timing decision (S-020.P03). Never stopping matters more than timing (S-050.P01).

rules.why_included: The home for 'no overrides'. The other rules survive a fall only if people follow them, and the library says execution and temperament separate outcomes more than rules do (S-046.P05). The limits are our conventions. It is not testable on prices.
rules.adopt_if: Adopted as a house practice: signed before any stock money. The monthly standing order starts now and does not wait for it. It stays while the journal shows no more than one departure in any 12 months. The engine does not check this; the household's own journal does.
rules.reject_if: Prices cannot reject it. Any change goes only through rule_change_protocol. A second departure in 12 months sells the pot into the index fund (back to paper, record kept). With no signed plan, no stock money moves, whatever the rule verdicts say.

rules.name: Rules change once a year, never after a fall, and every change is counted
rules.plain: Rules change only at the once-a-year review, with a written note, after waiting three months, and never while we are down 20% or more. Every change starts a fresh record and counts as one more try against luck. We keep the watchlist frozen.
rules.definition: Yearly review scores: did we follow the plan; real cost per trade against the engine's 10 bps (re-run if higher); the plan against the index fund alone; the fund's tracking and fees (S-017.P01). A change needs: a dated proposal in docs/decisions.md; 3 months of waiting; no change while the core or pot is down 20%+; 20 compliant decisions before a results-driven change; the effect surviving 20-25% nudges; a new rule id and forward record. A veto check run once on frozen settings is not a try; a variant whose result is read and then used to pick a setting, or any re-test after a frozen verdict, adds 1 to the tries count (17; by hand, no ledger yet). The program refuses a changed pre-registration unless tries_counted is raised. The 21-name watchlist and sector labels are frozen by agreement and the freeze hash; the engine has no add dates, so treat any addition as a rule change.

params.name: change window
params.why: Commit for years, not quarters (S-025.P03). Many people abandon a strategy in its losing stretch (S-003.P02).

params.name: waiting period
params.why: Our household convention. Untested.

params.name: fall freeze
params.value: no proposal or adoption while core or pot is -20% or worse
params.why: The household's 'never right after a drop', made checkable. A convention.

params.name: robustness
params.why: Shift settings by a fifth to a quarter; if the edge dies it was fitted (S-046.P03).

params.name: tries count
params.value: 17 now; +1 per variant read and used; no ledger yet
params.why: Search results must be corrected for the number tried (S-037.P01, S-037.P02); discount a record by the cohort it came from (S-032.P01). The engine reads only the number 17, and the freeze needs it raised after any change.

params.name: compliance first
params.value: 20 compliant decisions before a results-driven change
params.why: Our convention, borrowing the 20-sample floor of S-044.P02 (about judging an edge, not permitting rule changes).

params.name: real-cost re-run
params.value: if real cost is above 10 bps, recompute the verdict
params.why: A verdict holds only at the cost it assumed (S-020.P01, S-026.P05).

params.name: watchlist freeze
params.value: 21 names and sectors fixed; any addition is a rule change
params.why: Today's names were picked with hindsight. The freeze hash covers the list, but the engine has no add dates: a new name is pickable once it has a year of prices. General practice, not from the library.

rules.why_included: It guards against a well-documented failure: choosing rules after seeing results (S-037.P01, S-037.P02, S-032.P01). The sources are a few books and one large test, so the evidence is rated mixed; the waiting periods and the 20% freeze are our conventions. It also keeps the tries count honest.
rules.adopt_if: Adopted now. The tries ledger is NOT built: until it exists the number 17 is a fixed count in this file and every re-freeze needs a dated decisions.md entry. The program refuses a changed pre-registration unless tries_counted is raised. The rest is followed by people; the engine does not check it.
rules.reject_if: Prices cannot reject it; it changes only by its own procedure. A change made outside it voids that rule's record, which restarts from zero, and the change counts as a try.

rules.name: Index Only: everything in the core fund
rules.plain: The 'core' is the broad index fund: all the money goes into it and stays there. No stock picking. Every other plan must beat this after costs. It is also what stock-pot money does whenever no stock rule has earned trust.
rules.definition: Control, not a user rule. 100% in the core index fund (SPY proxy, adjusted closes so dividends count as reinvested), never sold by the control. In the satellite test it starts after the first trading year, pays one 10 bps entry cost, and fills at the next close. Its deepest drop is the yardstick for the rule 'deepest drop no more than 15 points worse than the core', and each rule's yearly-growth (CAGR) gap to it is printed. The savings arms buy this same fund. It is also the default plan: satellite money stays here until a satellite rule reaches passes_history AND meets every money condition in the acceptance text (the 182-day paper record is only one of them). During the paper record no money moves.

params.name: core fund
params.why: The repo's core proxy in config/settings.json.

params.name: satellite weight
params.why: The honest benchmark: investors as a group earn the market return minus costs (S-020.P01), and fund tables hide the losers (S-020.P05). Stock-pot money is at most 10% of savings, 2% per slot; the owner sets sizes.

params.name: trading cost
params.value: 10 bps (0.10%) per unit of weight traded
params.why: One entry cost in the control. Same cost rate as the rules.

params.name: drawdown yardstick
params.value: max 15 points worse than this control
params.why: Satellite acceptance number set by the registry owner. A rule that fails it cannot be passes_history.

params.name: not computed yet
params.why: Same dated contributions, with and without the satellite. Planned, not in the engine.

rules.why_included: Something simple must be the bar. Chart-based rules did not beat buy-and-hold after costs in the book's tests (S-021.P01) and the households that trade most earn less (S-021.P05), so the default when nothing passes is: do nothing special, stay in the index fund.
rules.adopt_if: Never adopted or dropped by a test; it is the yardstick and the default. Stock-pot money leaves it only when a stock rule passes history AND meets every money condition in the acceptance text, and the owner sets the size.
rules.reject_if: Not rejected by any result. Only the owner can move away from it, in writing, by choosing to fund a satellite.

rules.name: Whole list, equal shares (EW21)
rules.plain: Hold every name on our watchlist in equal shares, with no picking. A stock rule that cannot beat this has added nothing over simply owning the list. The list itself was chosen with hindsight, so this yardstick flatters.
rules.definition: Control, not a user rule. At the close of the first trading day of each month, hold every watchlist name that is eligible (253 trading days of history, so late listings join after a year), each in an equal share, no core fund and no leftover. Reset to equal at every monthly review. Fill at the next close. Cost 10 bps per unit of weight traded. Same start as the satellite rules. Today the engine prints each rule's yearly-growth (CAGR) gap to this control. It does NOT use that gap in the verdict. The pre-registered check 'beat EW21 by 1 point a year' is not computed yet.

params.name: names
params.why: No selection. A name counts only after 253 trading days of history.

params.name: sizing
params.why: Same as the rules' backtest sizing.

params.name: fill and cost
params.value: next close; 10 bps per unit of weight traded
params.why: Same as every rule.

params.name: hindsight
params.value: the list was chosen knowing today's winners
params.why: The list was chosen knowing today's winners, so this control probably flatters (survivorship, S-020.P05; history is a survivor's sample, S-032.P05). A rule is also tested against random baskets from the same list (control_random_basket).

params.name: not computed yet
params.why: Planned checks. Nothing in the engine reads as passed on them.

rules.why_included: It separates 'the rule picked well' from 'the list was already good'. The library has nothing on this yardstick, so it is untested as a method.
rules.adopt_if: Always run beside the satellite rules; never adopted. A rule is only worth following if it also beats the random baskets (verdict passes_history), and its gap to this control is read next to that.
rules.reject_if: Not rejected by any result. If a rule's CAGR gap to it is zero or negative, the rule has added nothing over owning the list. That is a reason to doubt it, but the engine verdict does not read this gap yet.

rules.name: Lucky dip: random names with the same rules
rules.plain: At every review, as many names as the rule holds (up to five) are drawn by lot from the same list, with the same replacement rate, caps, sizing, exits and costs. Done 2000 times. A rule that cannot beat these draws has shown only luck.
rules.definition: Control and the luck yardstick. 2000 draws, seed 20261005 (plus the draw number). At each decision day a draw holds as many names as the rule did, keeps each held name with the rule's own turnover rate if it is still eligible, and fills the rest from shuffled eligible names, using the rule's sector cap, sizing, exits, next-close fills and 10 bps cost. The rule's yearly growth (CAGR) is ranked among the draws, and also for each half of the period. p = (draws at or above the rule + 1) / 2001; adjusted p (stricter, for the 17 ideas tried) = p times 17, capped at 1. Verdicts: rejected below the 50th percentile; passes_history needs adjusted p of 0.05 or less (at most 4 of 2000 draws at or above the rule), 60+ in both halves, deepest drop no more than 15 points worse than the core, turnover at most 200% a year; candidate or inconclusive otherwise.

params.name: draws
params.why: The adjusted bar at 17 tries needs at least 339 draws to be reachable, so 2000 is enough. More draws (5000) when p is close are NOT done in the engine yet.

params.name: seed
params.why: Fixed before any run. Changing it would be a new try.

params.name: matched on
params.value: names held, replacement rate, sector cap, sizing, exits, fills, cost
params.why: Otherwise a slow-trading rule beats the null just by trading less.

params.name: bar
params.value: adjusted p 0.05 or less at 17 tries
params.why: Set by the registry owner. With 2000 draws that means at most 4 draws at or above the rule (about the 99.8th percentile). Percentile below 50 means rejected. 95 in the settings is the significance level, not the bar.

params.name: halves
params.why: Set by the registry owner. A rule must not rest on one stretch of years.

params.name: not computed yet
params.value: conditional, paired, sector-matched and planted-edge nulls; A/A calibration
params.why: Planned. Until the calibration passes, a satellite verdict says only what the engine computed, not that the pipeline is proven fair.

rules.why_included: Chart rules look good until the number tried is counted: the best of thousands tested on the S&P 500 was indistinguishable from luck (S-037.P01). Random picks from the same list are the fairest yardstick for luck (S-048.P01 tests rules against random entries). It is the main test for every satellite rule.
rules.adopt_if: Never adopted; it runs beside every satellite rule. A rule's fate depends on it: passes_history needs adjusted p of 0.05 or less, plus 60+ in each half, drawdown and turnover limits.
rules.reject_if: Not rejected. If the rule falls below the 50th percentile of the draws, the verdict is rejected. Between the bars it reads candidate or inconclusive, never adopted.

rules.name: Company numbers count only after they were published
rules.plain: A company's numbers count only from the day after it published them, as they were known then. They are never typed in by hand, remembered or supplied by the AI. Dormant: no data provider is approved, so nothing here runs today.
rules.definition: Dormant: the engine reads no company numbers today and the repo holds none. Each figure must come from the owner-approved provider with period end, filing date, form type and filing id. It counts from the first trading day after the filing date. If only the period end is known, add 41 days (quarterly report) or 61 days (annual report), then take the next trading day. On any date use the latest filing in force; restatements never rewrite the past. Delisted names must be included. Missing means fail; nothing is filled in. A filing older than 120 days is stale. A name needs 5 fiscal years of history. Financials and Utilities are out of scope. Before any result is read: check 3 names at 10 dates by hand against the filings, and re-run everything with every date pushed 30 days later.

params.name: effective date
params.value: first trading day after the filing date
params.why: A number cannot drive a decision before the public could see it. General practice, not from the library.

params.name: fallback lag
params.why: Based on the usual filing deadlines for large companies (40 and 60 days) plus one day. From general knowledge; to be checked with the provider.

params.name: stale after
params.why: General knowledge: the usual gap from a third-quarter filing to the annual one is about 112 days at the 40- and 60-day deadlines; 120 adds a week of margin.

params.name: restatements
params.value: as first reported; later changes never reach back
params.why: Using the latest corrected figure would show the past with knowledge nobody had then. General practice.

params.name: delisted names
params.why: Leaving out companies that failed makes any company-numbers test look better than it was (survivorship, S-020.P05).

params.name: minimum history
params.why: S-024.P01 asks for a history of operating profit; 5 years is our reading of that, not a tested figure.

params.name: timing stress
params.why: Our own check: a rule that only works with numbers earlier than they were public is peeking. Not computed today.

params.name: hand check
params.value: 3 names at 10 dates before any result
params.why: Catches wrong tag mapping or dates. Not computed today.

rules.data_needed: Point-in-time company statements: period end, filing date, form type, first-reported values, delisted names, 15+ years, split-adjusted shares. No provider is approved; the owner decides.
rules.why_included: Without this, any test on company numbers would peek at figures that were not public yet. It costs no counted try and moves no money. It is dormant because the house rule is to ask before choosing a data provider or adding a dependency.
rules.adopt_if: Adopted the day the owner approves a provider, as a precondition and not as a try. The provider must supply filing dates, first-reported values and delisted names, within its licence. The hand check (3 names, 10 dates) must match before any fundamental result is read.
rules.reject_if: The provider cannot supply filing dates, first-reported values or delisted names, or the hand check fails: that provider fails the contract. The fundamental rules then stay dormant or run by hand on the forward record only, never on 'latest value' data.

rules.name: Quality gate: steady cash profits, no quiet dilution
rules.plain: A veto, never a pick. Only hold a company with operating and cash profit in most recent years, at least 10% a year earned on shareholders' money, and no more than 2% new shares a year. Dormant until trusted company numbers exist.
rules.definition: Dormant: needs approved point-in-time data (fund_data_contract); the engine computes none of this today. At a review a name passes if, on figures in force that day: operating profit is positive in 4 of the last 5 years and in the last 12 months; operating cash flow is positive in 4 of 5 years and last-12-month free cash flow (cash flow minus capital spending) is positive; last-12-month cash flow is at least the reported profit; return on average shareholders' equity is at least 10% in 4 of 5 years; shares are up no more than 2% on a year ago. One failing report: no new buy, no sale. A second failing report in a row: the name leaves at the next review. Financials and Utilities are out of scope. It only removes names; it never ranks them.

params.name: history tests
params.why: S-024.P01 says 'most years'. 4 of 5 is our reading of that, not a tested number.

params.name: return on equity floor
params.why: S-024.P01. The 15% moat figure in S-024.P02 is not used. Very high returns often mean heavy debt (S-024.P02): a floor, never a rank. No debt test here, so ROE can be debt-flattered.

params.name: cash conversion
params.value: last-12-month cash flow / profit at least 1.0
params.why: S-024.P03 calls cash flow drifting away from profit an early warning. The 1.0 cut-off is our choice and untested.

params.name: dilution cap
params.why: S-024.P06 names about 2% a year as quiet dilution. Applied to all names, not only those without acquisitions.

params.name: free cash flow floor
params.why: S-024.P01 lists positive free cash flow in its screen. The cut-off is untested.

params.name: exit confirmation
params.why: Sell for business reasons, not price (S-023.P04, S-027.P02). Requiring two in a row is our convention to avoid one-off noise.

params.name: role
params.why: S-024.P01's screen has no quality ranking; S-025.P01 ranks on return on capital, used only in rung C. No test exists here, so the evidence is weak.

rules.data_needed: Approved point-in-time statements: operating profit, operating and free cash flow, net profit, shareholders' equity, diluted shares, for 5+ fiscal years, delisted names included.
rules.why_included: Most of the library's company screen (S-024.P01), made exact. It leaves out the clean-balance-sheet test, so a return on equity of 10% can still come from debt (S-024.P02); that gap is open and the owner may add a debt test before data is approved. It removes names rather than picking them. The library gives no tested hit rate, so the evidence is weak.
rules.adopt_if: After a provider is approved, on a broad universe with delisted names (15+ years): the share of names losing over half within 12 months must be lower than in at least 95% of random baskets, and hold with dates +30 days. Then it joins rung B and needs passes_history there. The engine computes none of this yet.
rules.reject_if: It fails either test, fails the +30-day delay, or the hand check in fund_data_contract fails. Inconclusive counts as rejected. Rejected means dropped, never loosened or tightened after seeing results.

rules.name: Sales per share growing at least 3% a year
rules.plain: The owner's own idea. Only hold a company whose sales per share are up at least 3% a year over the latest year and over three years. A floor that keeps out firms with flat or slow sales per share, never a reason to prefer fast growers. Dormant until data exists.
rules.definition: Dormant: needs approved point-in-time data; the engine computes none of this today. Sales per share = last-12-month sales divided by diluted average shares, split-adjusted. g1 is its growth against a year ago. g3 is its yearly growth rate over 3 years. A name passes if both are at least 3%. If either cannot be worked out, it fails. It is a veto, never a rank. It sits behind fund_quality_gate, because buybacks can lift sales per share while the business shrinks. A held name leaves after 2 failing reports in a row. Retirement rule, fixed now: if on the watchlist the floor changes who is eligible in fewer than 1 name-month in 10, it is called inert and deleted, never tightened.

params.name: growth floor
params.why: Our own number, no source. It echoes the 3% terminal growth that S-024.P04 uses when discounting free cash flows: a valuation assumption, not evidence about sales or filters. Untested.

params.name: windows
params.value: last year AND 3-year rate, both required
params.why: Our choice: a fast but noisy window and a slow but stale one guard each other. Untested.

params.name: role
params.why: S-023.P06 shows overpaying for great growers lost money; it does not say growth is fully priced in. The library has no tested evidence that fast growers do better (S-029.P05), so no ranking.

params.name: share basis
params.why: Per-share counts dilution (S-024.P06). But buybacks lift it too, and S-013.P01 rates growth from a lower share count weaker than revenue growth, which is why this sits behind fund_quality_gate. The owner's choice of per-share is untested.

params.name: retirement
params.value: inert if it changes eligibility in under 1 name-month in 10
params.why: An inert rule cannot be tested and would only add a try.

params.name: exit confirmation
params.why: The same convention as fund_quality_gate.

rules.data_needed: Approved point-in-time quarterly sales and diluted average share counts, 4 years or more, split-adjusted, delisted names included.
rules.why_included: The owner's own example of a company-number test. The library has nothing that tests it, so it is labelled untested, kept as a veto only and placed behind the quality gate. S-029.P05 reminds us such thresholds are a discipline, not a tested signal.
rules.adopt_if: On a broad point-in-time universe, names failing the floor lose over half within 12 months more often than names passing it (calendar-year windows, bootstrap). It is not inert on the watchlist and holds with dates +30 days. Then it joins rung B. The engine computes none of this yet.
rules.reject_if: Inert by the retirement rule: deleted. No difference on the broad universe, or the +30-day delay breaks it: not used. Inconclusive counts as rejected. The floor is never tightened after seeing results.

rules.name: Numbers allow, price confirms: the three-rung ladder
rules.plain: A company must first be allowed by its numbers, then confirmed by its price. Neither can buy alone. Only if a test shows it helps do we also prefer firms that are good value for their quality. Dormant until data exists.
rules.definition: Dormant: the engine runs only rung A today (five_leaders, price only). At each review, with figures in force that day: 1) Scope: watchlist minus Financials and Utilities (rungs B, C). 2) Numbers allow (B, C): fund_quality_gate and fund_rps_growth both pass. 3) Price confirms: the Five Leaders entry tests (above a rising 200-day line, not stretched). 4) Rank by 12-month return skipping the latest month. Rung C only: add the earnings-yield and return-on-capital ranks to the price rank (three ranks, equal weight); best total wins, ties to the better price rank. 5) 1 name per sector, 5 slots, equal at each review in tests. A held name leaves after 2 failing reports in a row, below its 200-day line at a review, or out of the top 10. Valuation never causes an exit. Ladder: A price only; B adds step 2; C adds the value-and-quality rank.

params.name: order
params.value: numbers veto, then price veto, then rank
params.why: Numbers must pass before price can confirm; neither buys alone. Never buy a sound business only because its price rose (S-022.P06). That source also says never sell on a price fall; our 200-day exit departs from it. S-025.P01 does not test this order: it combines two value-and-quality ranks only.

params.name: rank weights
params.value: equal weight: price rank + earnings-yield rank + return-on-capital rank
params.why: S-025.P01 adds only the last two ranks. Adding the price rank is our design and untested (value and quality get 2/3 of the weight; the owner confirms). Ties go to the better price rank.

params.name: value-and-quality rank
params.value: earnings yield + return on capital, ranks added
params.why: Earnings yield = operating profit / enterprise value. Return on capital = operating profit / (working capital + fixed assets). Never EBITDA (S-024.P03). Untested here.

params.name: scope
params.value: Financials and Utilities out of rungs B and C
params.why: S-025.P02 excludes them from the earnings-yield and return-on-capital ranks (rung C). For rung B it is our choice: operating profit and cash flow are not comparable for banks, insurers and regulated utilities. The owner may keep a price-only slot for them.

params.name: ladder stopping rule
params.value: C only if it beats B above the 95th percentile of a paired null; else B; if B fails, A
params.why: Fixed now so a good decade cannot pick the winner afterwards (S-037.P02). The paired null is not in the engine yet.

params.name: tries counted
params.value: rung A is the Five Leaders try; B and C are 2 more
params.why: Each rung is a counted try against luck (S-037.P01). All count inside the one global total of 17.

params.name: long-run caution
params.why: The library's formula lagged the market about one year in four and its edge narrowed after publication. Expect the same humility.

rules.data_needed: Everything in fund_data_contract, plus enterprise value, working capital, fixed assets and unadjusted prices, on a broad point-in-time universe with delisted names.
rules.why_included: The only proposal that answers how company numbers and price fit together, and its ladder keeps every added test an explicit counted try. Rung A is testable today; B and C stay dormant until the owner approves data.
rules.adopt_if: B (or C) must reach passes_history on a broad point-in-time universe (15+ years, delisted names): adjusted p <= 0.05, both halves at or above the 60th percentile, drop within 15 points of the core, turnover at most 200% a year, and hold with dates +30 days. C only if it beats B per the stopping rule. Money also needs forward record.
rules.reject_if: B fails passes_history: keep A or nothing. C not above the 95th percentile over B: keep B. A rung that needs numbers earlier than they were public is rejected as peeking. Inconclusive counts as rejected, and the pot stays in the index fund.

sets.name: Monthly Autopilot
sets.plain: The core plan, usable now with no paper period. Every payday a standing order buys the index fund. Money already in hand goes in all at once. Nothing is sold in a fall, and rules change only at the yearly review.

sets.name: Five Leaders
sets.plain: The small stock pot, testable on prices today. The main rule holds up to five names, one per sector, ranked by their past year, above a rising 200-day line and not stretched. Two variants are tested beside it: one without the 200-day line, one reviewed quarterly. The pot is at most a tenth of savings.

sets.name: The Patient Household
sets.plain: The whole trader today: Monthly Autopilot for the savings plus Five Leaders for the small pot. The pot stays in the index fund until Five Leaders beats random picks in history and then earns a paper record. If it never does, nothing changes.

sets.name: The Patient Household, Checked Books
sets.plain: The same trader once trustworthy company accounts exist: a company must pass its numbers (cash profits, no quiet dilution, sales per share up at least 3% a year) before its price counts. Dormant until the owner approves a data provider. Nothing in it is tested yet.

sets.name: Index Only
sets.plain: Everything in the index fund, with the same payday purchases and no stock picking. Every plan must beat it after costs, and it is what we do whenever nothing else earns a place.

sets.name: Yardsticks: Rule v1, Lucky Dip, All 21
sets.plain: The tape measures, not plans. Rule v1 is the stock rule the site already runs. The lucky dip draws, by lot, as many names as the rule held at each review (same replacement rate, caps, sizes and costs). All 21 is every eligible watchlist name held equally. A new rule must beat the lucky dips.

experiments.question: Before any rule result is opened: does the verdict code call pure luck skilled no more often than its bar says, and how small a yearly edge could it ever see?
experiments.method: Planned, not computed yet: (1) run 200 random-pick pseudo-rules in the Five Leaders frame through the full verdict code, each against its own random baskets, judged at 1 try and at 17 tries. (2) Find the smallest yearly edge the history sees 80% of the time. (3) Plant known edges of 2, 4, 6 and 8 points a year and count how often they are found. Today only the repo tests check that a random picker is not called skilled more often than chance.
experiments.null_model: The random baskets themselves: a random picker's percentile should be spread evenly from low to high.
experiments.pass_criteria: Planned requirement: 4 to 16 false 'skilled' calls out of 200 at 1 try, at most 2 out of 200 at 17 tries (a correct pipeline expects 0.6 and exceeds 2 about 2% of the time), percentiles spread evenly. If it fails, no satellite verdict is trusted. The smallest visible edge is shown next to every verdict. If it is bigger than the gap between the goal and the core, the site says history cannot see an edge that size.
metrics: false positives out of 200 at 1 try and at 17 tries
spread of percentiles in ten bands
smallest yearly edge seen 80% of the time (1, 6 and 17 tries)
share of planted edges found (2, 4, 6, 8 points a year)
years of forward record needed to see a 3 and a 5 point edge

experiments.question: For the salary stream, does buying the core fund every 1, 2 or 13 weeks differ materially from every 4 weeks in money-weighted return? (No trading cost is charged in the savings test; the fee at which two cadences tie is printed.)
experiments.method: Runs today: one unit of cash arrives each week; everything on hand is invested every x weeks (x = 1, 2, 4 baseline, 13). Waiting cash earns the T-bill fund (zero before it existed). Fills at the next close, no trading cost charged (the break-even fee per order is printed). Rolling starts every 4 weeks over 52, 104 and 156 weeks, each paired with the 4-week baseline by start date. Independent windows = span divided by horizon. Not computed yet: other start offsets, a T-bill-era split, regret, days to recover, fixed-fee scenarios beyond the break-even fee.
experiments.null_model: The every-4-weeks baseline on the same stream, costs and fills.
experiments.pass_criteria: [engine] A cadence is 'better' only with at least 8 independent windows, a median gain of at least 50 bps a year and better in at least 80% of starts. Otherwise no_clear_difference (expected), worse or too_few_independent_windows, and monthly stays. Likely only the 52-week row has enough windows. [planned] Same sign at 104 and 156 weeks; worst moment no more than 2 points worse; the broker's real fee below the printed break-even fee for weekly and 2-weekly, above it for quarterly.
metrics: median money-weighted return difference vs baseline (bps a year)
share of starts better than baseline
independent windows
median, 10th and 90th percentile money multiple
10th percentile of the worst moment below money paid in
average share held in cash
orders per year
break-even fee per order (share of one weekly payment)

experiments.question: For money already in hand, how much does staging over 26 or 52 weeks give up against investing all at once?
experiments.method: Runs today: a windfall of 100 units arrives on day one and is invested at once (baseline) or in equal weekly parts over 26 or 52 weeks. Idle money earns the T-bill fund. Fills at the next close, no trading cost charged. No break-even fee is printed for these arms (only the salary-stream arms have one), rolling starts every 4 weeks over 52, 104 and 156 weeks, paired with the lump sum by start date. Independent windows = span divided by horizon. Not computed yet: break-even fee, other start offsets, a T-bill-era split, regret.
experiments.null_model: Lump sum at once, with the same costs and fills.
experiments.pass_criteria: [engine] Staging is 'better' only with at least 8 independent windows, a median gain of at least 50 bps a year and better in at least 80% of starts; otherwise no_clear_difference, worse or too_few_independent_windows, and the lump sum stays. [planned] Any staging result is shown to the owner as the price of comfort, never as timing skill.
metrics: median money-weighted return difference vs lump sum (bps a year)
share of starts better than the lump sum
independent windows
median, 10th and 90th percentile money multiple
10th percentile of the worst moment below money paid in
average share held in cash

experiments.question: Does the 12-1 ranking (five_leaders_m1), or that ranking plus the 200-day line (five_leaders), pick better names than random baskets, and where does rule v1 sit on the same yardstick?
experiments.method: Runs today: after a 253-day warm-up, each rule is simulated with monthly decisions on that day's data, next-close fills, 10 bps, names joining after 253 days, unfilled slots in the core. Each is compared with 2000 random baskets (seed 20261005) with the same number of names at every decision, replacement rate, caps, sizing, exits and costs, with p adjusted for 17 tries. Controls: core only and all 21 names equal. The verdict is read once and frozen. Not computed yet: conditional or paired nulls, crash checks.
experiments.null_model: control_random_basket: same names pool, same count, replacement rate, caps, sizing, exits, fills and costs; only which names differs.
experiments.pass_criteria: [engine] The verdict word set by the [engine] items in the acceptance text: passes_history, candidate, inconclusive or rejected. v1 is capped at candidate. [planned] Gaps to the core and to all 21 are shown but not in the verdict yet. Whether the 200-day line helps (five_leaders against five_leaders_m1) needs a paired test that is not built.
metrics: growth rate after costs (CAGR) and its percentile among the random baskets
one-sided p and p adjusted for 17 tries
percentile in each half of the history
growth gap vs the core and vs all 21 (points a year)
deepest drop vs the core (points)
turnover a year, stops included
average names held and decisions made
random baskets' 5th, 50th and 95th percentile growth

experiments.question: On the same picks, does the household practice (equal at entry, no top-ups, winners drift) cost anything against resetting to equal at every review?
experiments.method: Planned, not computed yet: needs engine work. Run Five Leaders with drift sizing (no resets, no top-ups, a 25% trim back to 20%) against the same rule with the monthly equal reset that every backtest uses today. The random baskets must drift the same way, paired draw by draw. Until it is built, backtests describe the reset rule, not the household practice.
experiments.null_model: The same sizing switch applied to the random baskets, paired draw by draw.
experiments.pass_criteria: Planned requirement: drift stays the household practice. It is dropped only if its deepest drop is more than 5 points worse than the reset version AND it saves less than 40% of the trading, at 10 bps, in both halves. Build this before any money (see open questions).
metrics: change in growth rate at 10 and 30 bps
change in deepest drop
change in turnover
trims per year
largest single-name weight reached
percentile of the rule's change among the paired draws

experiments.question: Is a quarterly review of Five Leaders no worse than a monthly one, at lower turnover?
experiments.method: Runs today: five_leaders (monthly) and five_leaders_quarterly (first trading day of Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct) run in the same frame at 10 bps. Each is judged against its own 2000 random baskets drawn on its own decision days, with p adjusted for 17 tries. Both rows show percentile, turnover, drop and growth. The choice between them is made by people reading the two rows, not by code.
experiments.null_model: Random baskets matched to each cadence's own decisions, names held and replacement rate.
experiments.pass_criteria: [engine] Each cadence gets its own verdict. [planned, read by people] Only a passes_history version is used. If only one passes, that one is used. If monthly and quarterly both pass: quarterly only when its percentile is within 10 points of monthly and its turnover is at most 60% of monthly, else monthly. If the basic version and the main version both pass, the owner reads the two rows side by side and writes the choice down.
metrics: percentile among random baskets, each cadence
turnover a year
growth rate after costs
deepest drop vs the core
decisions made

experiments.question: Is a passing satellite rule a broad plateau or a lucky spike: do nearby settings, other review days and a later fill behave similarly?
experiments.method: Planned, not computed yet: for every rule at candidate or better, move one setting at a time by about a fifth to a quarter (lookback 252 to 200 or 315; skipped month 21 to 17 or 26; keep rank 10 to 8 or 12; stretch 8% to 6% or 10%; 200-day line to 150, 160 or 250; slope window 21 to 17 or 26). Also slots 5 to 4, sector cap 1 to 2, review on trading day 1, 6, 11 and 16, and a fill 5 days late. Each variant gets its own random baskets. Veto only. Run once on the frozen settings, so not a try; a variant whose result is read and then used to pick a setting counts as one (rule_change_protocol).
experiments.null_model: Each neighbour, review day and fill delay gets its own random baskets.
experiments.pass_criteria: Planned requirement: at least 75% of neighbours at percentile 70 or more, none below 50, the centre no more than 15 points above the neighbour median, all four review days at 70 or more. A neighbour median below 50 means REJECT. A rule that fails with a 5-day fill window shrinks its order window to the next close.
metrics: lowest and median neighbour percentile
share of neighbours at percentile 70 or more
centre minus neighbour median
percentile at each review day
percentile with a 5-day fill delay

experiments.question: How much of a result comes from knowing today which 21 names became big winners, rather than from the rule?
experiments.method: Planned, not computed yet: (1) hindsight bonus = all-21 growth minus a broad equal-weight fund's growth; subtract it from the rule. (2) Leave one name out, 21 reruns, for the rule and its random baskets. (3) Drop the top 1, 2 and 3 names. (4) A stale-signal placebo ranking by the return from 24 to 12 months ago. (5) A look-ahead ceiling shown only as an upper bound. (6) Sector-matched baskets. The all-21 gap is shown today; the rest is new engine work.
experiments.null_model: Random baskets redone on each changed list of names; the stale-signal placebo is a rule that can only profit from hindsight.
experiments.pass_criteria: Planned requirement before any money: leave-one-out minimum percentile 60 or more; dropping the best name keeps 80 or more; the placebo at least 20 points below the rule; top name under half of the excess; hindsight-adjusted growth at least the core's. REJECT if the placebo is within 5 points or dropping the best name leaves under 50.
metrics: hindsight bonus (points a year)
hindsight-adjusted growth vs the core
lowest leave-one-out percentile
percentile after dropping the top 1, 2, 3 names
placebo percentile and its gap to the rule
sector-matched percentile
top name's share of the excess

experiments.question: Is the result spread across time and market conditions, or carried by one stretch?
experiments.method: Partly runs today: the engine already gives the percentile in each half of the history, and the verdict uses it. Planned, not computed yet: percentiles for odd and even years, rising and falling core, calm and wild months, the deepest core falls (depth and days to recover against the core and the random median), calendar years ahead of the random median, and excess with the best 2 years removed.
experiments.null_model: The random baskets restricted to the same months as each bucket.
experiments.pass_criteria: [engine] Percentile of 60 or more in both halves is needed for passes_history; the engine does not check the other splits. [planned] Ahead of the random median in at least 6 of about 9 calendar years; excess still positive without the best 2 years; below the 25th percentile in either half or in odd or even years means REJECT. REJECT if the deepest drop is more than 25 points worse than the core.
metrics: percentile in each half (computed today)
percentile in odd and even years
excess in each market condition
depth and recovery in the deepest core falls
calendar years ahead of the random median
excess without the best 2 years

experiments.question: Does a satellite result survive higher trading costs?
experiments.method: Planned, not computed yet: today the engine runs one cost, 10 bps per unit of weight traded. Planned: re-run every candidate at 10, 20, 30 and 50 bps with its random baskets at the same cost, and find the cost where its percentile falls to 50 and where its edge over all 21 reaches zero. Taxes are not modelled, so turnover stands in for them.
experiments.null_model: The random baskets at the same cost.
experiments.pass_criteria: Planned requirement before any money: percentile 90 or more at 30 bps and break-even cost against all 21 of at least 50 bps. REJECT if the percentile is below 50 at 20 bps or turnover is above 400% of the pot a year. [engine] The turnover limit (at most 200% a year) is checked today at 10 bps. Rule v1 is recorded at 419.6% a year counting buys and sells, about 210% replaced.
metrics: percentile and growth gap vs all 21 at each cost
break-even cost where percentile reaches 50
break-even cost vs all 21
turnover a year

experiments.question: Given every variant tried, is the best satellite rule distinguishable from the best of the same number of luck-only rules?
experiments.method: Partly runs today: every satellite row carries a one-sided p adjusted for the 17 tries counted (Bonferroni), with 2000 random baskets, which is enough to reach the bar. Planned, not computed yet: an append-only tries ledger of every setting whose result is viewed, White's Reality Check on monthly excess over all 21 (block bootstrap), and a deflated Sharpe ratio. The count of 17 includes reserved arms the engine cannot run yet.
experiments.null_model: The best of 17 luck-only rules, through Bonferroni's union bound and, later, a bootstrap.
experiments.pass_criteria: [engine] p adjusted for 17 tries of 0.05 or less (with 2000 baskets: at most 4 at or above the rule, about the 99.8th percentile). [planned] Reality Check p of 0.10 or less at 6-month blocks and 0.15 or less at 3 and 12; deflated Sharpe ratio 0.95 or more.
metrics: tries counted
p adjusted for tries (computed today)
Reality Check p at 3, 6 and 12 month blocks
deflated Sharpe ratio per rule

experiments.question: What does the whole household account look like with a 10% stock pot run by the rule, against Index Only and against random pots, and how often does the 15% band fire?
experiments.method: Planned, not computed yet: a household-account wrapper. The monthly stream goes into the core; a pot of 10% of investable savings is funded once and run by Five Leaders, and by 200 matched random pots. Yearly check at 15% with a trim back to 10% (a house convention reusing the 5-point stock/bond band of S-022.P04; descriptive only, with and without the trim). Money-weighted and time-weighted results are shown apart and never mixed.
experiments.null_model: Index Only with the same payments, and random pots in the same 90/10 mix.
experiments.pass_criteria: Planned requirement: descriptive only. It never gives a verdict on a rule. It shows the owner how far a 10% pot can move the household before the size is confirmed. Using the +20% goal as a pass or fail test is forbidden.

deepest drop of the household account

range across random pots

experiments.question: Once a data provider is approved: do the quality gate and the sales-per-share floor, then the value-and-quality rank, add to price-only Five Leaders without look-ahead?
experiments.method: Planned, not computed yet: blocked until the owner approves a provider; no fundamentals data exists in the repo. Order: data checks (hand reconciliation, coverage by sector, a 30-day delay stress), pass rates and an inert-floor test, a broad point-in-time universe that includes delisted names, then rung B (gate and floor) and rung C (rank) against random baskets with a paired null. Rungs B and C are two counted tries.
experiments.null_model: Random baskets from the names that pass the fundamental tests, and from the full scope; a paired null for rung C against rung B.
experiments.pass_criteria: Planned requirement: the fundamental rules' adopt_if and the ladder rule. If the gate or floor passes 80% or more of the 21 names in most months, the watchlist result is not evidence and only the broad-universe result counts. Any result that fails the 30-day delay stress is rejected as look-ahead.

coverage by sector
