experiments.question: On prices it has never seen, does each tracked satellite rule behave as its history promised, and does the household follow the plan without overrides?
experiments.method: Partly runs today: the forward ledger (paper_rules.json) records each tracked rule's holdings on the first run of each review month with that day's data, never edited. A rule whose settings change starts a new record and the old one is kept. Each track is replayed by the same engine and, after 6 decisions and 126 trading days, compared with random baskets on the recorded days (forward percentile). Planned: scoring orders from the private journal, deviation counts, a band from history, demotion tests. Overrides reset a rule's record (people enforce this).
experiments.null_model: Random baskets over the forward window only. Their percentile is spread evenly when there is no skill, so a short record proves little on its own.
experiments.pass_criteria: [engine] Forward percentile appears once a rule has 6 decisions AND a track over 126 trading days (about 7 monthly decisions; 12 to 15 months quarterly). [planned] Money for a passes_history rule needs every condition in the acceptance list. A candidate moves up after 24 months at forward percentile 80+. Demotion: forward percentile under 20 after 24 months, or excess under the historical 5th percentile.
metrics: days and decisions recorded (computed today)
forward percentile vs random baskets (computed today)
forward excess vs all 21 and vs the core
position inside the historical 12-month excess band
forward deepest drop vs the historical worst
share of orders placed on time and deviations
gap between the real account and the paper track

adopt: Status of every check below is as of 2026-10-05: 'program' (tagged [engine]) means the program computes it on every daily run; 'planned' means written down now, not built yet, so people check it by hand before any money. The page header shows whether real prices have been run.

[engine] passes_history (a first screen: it opens no money) needs ALL of: adjusted p of 0.05 or less (17 tries, 2000 random baskets: at most 4 baskets at or above the rule, p = (count+1)/2001 times 17, about the 99.8th percentile); at least the 60th percentile in BOTH halves of the history; deepest drop no more than 15 points worse than the core; turnover at most 200% a year.

[engine] Turnover is the percent of the stock pot replaced per year (a sale and a purchase count once), equal-weight resets and stops included. Rule v1: the site's record is 419.6% counting buys and sells (about 210% on this basis, shorter window, same-close fills); the engine prints its own figure, which may land above or below 200%.

[engine] Test conditions are fixed: decisions on the first trading day of the month (quarter for the quarterly arm) plus one on the first test day, on that day's data; fills at the next close; 10 bps per unit of weight traded; names join after 253 trading days of unbroken prices (a missing bar, or a name with no price on the last day, stops the run); random-draw seed 20261005.

[engine] The program reads one number, tries_counted = 17; the split is counted by hand (no ledger yet). A 'try' is every variant we run or hold in reserve. 7 are savings plans, 6 are stock-rule variants (one, drift sizing, in reserve), 4 are held in reserve for checks not built yet (the household account 2, the two fundamental rungs 1 each). 7 + 6 + 4 = 17.

[engine] The history verdict is read once, on the first real-price run, and frozen. Later days update displayed numbers only. A change to a rule's engine settings, to the settings rule v1 reads, to the watchlist or its sector labels, to an acceptance number, the cost or the tries starts a new freeze; the program accepts it only if tries_counted was raised, and keeps the old freeze in the file.

[planned] The freeze hash does not cover the wording of the money gates and vetoes, or the engine code: public git history protects them. Any change to them after the first real-data run needs a dated decisions.md entry and +1 try.

[engine] A savings arm replaces its baseline only when its verdict is 'better' (8+ independent windows, median gain of 50 bps a year or more, better in 80% or more of rolling starts; quarterly may also win on a broker fee above its printed break-even fee), then through rule_change_protocol. Only the 52-week row can reach a verdict; 104 and 156 weeks show the sign only.

[planned] Money for a passes_history rule needs ALL of: 182+ paper days (calendar days), forward percentile 50 or more, 100% on-time orders, growth after costs ahead of the core and all 21 names (the owner reads the printed gaps), the E06-E10 vetoes once built, the owner's size within 10%. No code enforces this. The forward gate is a sanity check: about half of luck-only rules pass percentile 50.
[planned] The core plan (monthly autopilot, cash windfall in one go) is adopted now. It needs no paper period, and no test result can pause the monthly purchase.

[planned] Stability and hindsight checks (E06-E08): at least 75% of neighbouring settings at percentile 70 or more, none below 50; best name removed keeps 80; leave-one-out minimum 60; placebo 20 points lower; ahead of the random median in at least 6 of 9 years. Until they run, passes_history is a first screen only.

[planned] Family-wise and cost checks (E09, E10): Reality Check p of 0.10 or less at 6-month blocks and 0.15 or less at 3 and 12, deflated Sharpe ratio 0.95 or more, percentile 90 or more at 30 bps, break-even cost against all 21 of at least 50 bps. The engine runs only 10 bps and the Bonferroni check.
[planned] E00 calibration passes first. Today a small repo test (12 random pickers, 80 draws each, at most 3 tail results) guards only against gross miscalibration; it does not test the 17-try bar.

[planned] Components stay only on their own tests: the 200-day line (five_leaders against five_leaders_m1, paired), drift against reset (E04), quarterly against monthly (E05). They are credited for risk or cost, never for picking skill. For now the rows are shown side by side.

[planned] Savings extras: same sign at 52, 104 and 156 weeks; worst moment no more than 2 points worse; a T-bill-era run; the broker's real fee per order against the printed break-even fee (printed for salary-stream arms; the broker fee is not in the system).
[planned] At least 30 distinct position entries over the history, so a result does not rest on a handful of trades. The engine counts decisions, not entries.

[planned] Fundamental rungs (dormant): the same satellite numbers, first on a broad point-in-time universe, surviving a 30-day data delay. Rung C needs the 95th percentile over rung B on a paired null.

[planned] House rules stay in force while a rule is under test: docs/household.md rule 2 (3 of 4 setup checks), rule 3 (no entries near earnings or macro events), rule 4 (no averaging down 'by default') and the trust ladder describe rule v1. Rule 3 conflicts with 'orders are exactly the rule's list'; they must be rewritten with a change note before any money follows Five Leaders.
candidate: [engine] candidate: not rejected, unadjusted p of 0.05 or less (beat about 95% of random baskets) and the 60th percentile or better in both halves, but the adjusted-p bar, the drop limit or the turnover limit is missed.

[engine] The forward ledger records every tracked satellite rule from its first run, whatever its verdict. A candidate has no plan role and no money. It is a rule worth watching on the forward record.
[engine] baseline_portfolio_v1 is capped at candidate: its history was seen before this registry was written, so its best possible verdict is candidate.
[planned] Any other rule whose real-price history was viewed before registration is capped at candidate too; so is a rule with a regime or crash-month weakness once those checks exist.

[planned] A candidate moves toward money only after at least 24 months of forward record with forward percentile of 80 or more, 100% on-time orders, and the risk and cost limits still met. The ledger computes the forward percentile; people check the rest.
[engine] A savings arm that leans better but misses 50 bps or the 80% share is reported as no_clear_difference. The baseline stays. [planned] A re-test later is a new counted try.
reject: [engine] rejected: below the 50th percentile of the matched random baskets (it beat fewer than half of them).
[engine] inconclusive (neither rejected, candidate nor passes_history) is treated as not adopted. Satellite money stays in the core fund. It stays a counted try and is re-tested only on new data.
[engine] A savings arm with verdict 'worse' (median loss of 50 bps or more, better in 20% or fewer of starts) is rejected, and the baseline stays.
[planned] Either half, or odd years or even years, below the 25th percentile; neighbour median percentile below 50 (E06, E08).
[planned] Percentile below 50 at 20 bps, or turnover above 400% a year (E09). The engine already blocks passes_history above 200% a year.

[planned] Hindsight failure: percentile below 50 with the best name removed, or the placebo within 5 points of the rule (E07). Risk failure: deepest drop more than 25 points worse than the core. The engine already blocks passes_history beyond 15 points.
[planned] The rule cannot be written as code, or needs a judgment call (S-037.P03).
[planned] Pipeline failure: if E00 fails, no satellite verdict is trusted until the pipeline is fixed.

[planned] Forward demotion: forward percentile below 20 after 24 months, or forward 12-month excess below the historical 5th percentile. An override or late order resets the record; a second one in 12 months sells the pot into the index fund (back to paper, record kept).
[planned] Stock pot sunset: after 36 months funded, if the pot's money-weighted return is below the core's over the same dated flows, the pot closes and the money goes back to the core.
[planned] Fundamental rules: a result that fails the 30-day delay stress or the hand check is rejected as look-ahead. A sales-per-share floor that changes almost nothing is deleted, never tightened.

not_supported.name: Pause savings while the core is weak (left-out gate 1)
not_supported.why: Not registered, which saves a try. It conflicts with the never-stop evidence (S-050.P01, S-007.P03), and 2 or 3 market falls cannot support a test. The owner may register it at an annual review.

not_supported.name: Move satellite slots to the core when the core is weak (left-out gate 2)
not_supported.why: Not registered. It uses the same core-weakness signal as gate 1 on the same few market falls. It removes single-name risk, not market risk, and overlaps the 200-day line in Five Leaders.

not_supported.name: Freeze new buys after a 20% pot fall (left-out gate 3)
not_supported.why: Not registered. It borrows a rule for leveraged trading accounts (S-040.P03) for a five-name pot, would fire only a few times a decade, and overlaps the drawdown playbook.

not_supported.name: Drift sizing and the 25% trim (until the engine supports them)
not_supported.why: This is the household practice: equal at entry, no top-ups, winners drift. Backtests reset to equal at every review. The drift arm (E04) is reserved and needs engine work before any money.

not_supported.name: Daily stops and daily trend-break exits
not_supported.why: Not run. S-050.P07 itself says to exit on any daily close below the long average; we deliberately check on review days only, a house convention (no orders between reviews), and a break may be held up to a month. S-046.P04 found added stops hurt slow systems, which is not the same test. No hard stop on an unleveraged pot is the shelf's reading (docs/shelf.md), not S-034.P03.

not_supported.name: Entry on a 252-day-high breakout
not_supported.why: Low prior: breakout edges decayed to chance (S-048.P01). It mostly picks the same names as 12-1 ranking, and buying at highs is hard to follow.

not_supported.name: Entry on a pullback to the 200-day line
not_supported.why: The library source prefers this entry in a rising uptrend (S-050.P06, no backtest, S-050.P11), so it is not silent. Not registered: entries just above the exit line would whip in and out, it adds a try, and buying on a dip is a different rule from 12-1 ranking. The owner may register it at the annual review.

not_supported.name: A separate test of the stretch veto
not_supported.why: The veto is kept as a temperament rule whatever a test shows, so a test could not change a decision and would only spend a try.

not_supported.name: Correlation cap for the new rules
not_supported.why: Five Leaders has no correlation cap. The price provider's correlations look implausibly low (docs/decisions.md), and correlations go to one in a panic (S-034.P02). Rule v1 keeps its cap unchanged.

not_supported.name: Inverse-volatility sizing
not_supported.why: The engine can run it, but it is not registered: no library evidence for an unstopped five-name pot, it tilts toward calm names, and volatility is not risk (S-026.P02).

not_supported.name: Rank by 3 or 6 months alone, lookback scanning, 52-week-high ranking, sector rotation
not_supported.why: Redundant with the 12-1 ranking or with v1. Scanning lookbacks is the data-mining trap (S-037.P01). Nearby settings are tried only as veto checks (E06).

not_supported.name: Weekly or quarterly buying as the core plan; value averaging; buying extra after falls
not_supported.why: Weekly, every 2 weeks and quarterly buying run only as report-only arms (E01). Value averaging needs unbounded payments after falls. Dip-buying needs an untested trigger (S-007.P02, S-047.P02).

not_supported.name: A 90/10 split of every payment into the pot
not_supported.why: A recurring top-up conflicts with S-022.P01 (speculation capped and never topped up), buys the pot after losses and muddies the forward record. Kept as an owner option in the open questions.

not_supported.name: Chart patterns, volume bases, candlesticks, crossovers, oscillators, support and resistance
not_supported.why: Not codable without judgment (S-037.P03), or no volume data in the engine. Objective chart rules tried in bulk showed no edge once tries were counted (S-037.P01); volume signals failed as triggers (S-038.P02). S-048.P01 found crossovers only marginally better than chance and S-041.P05 says published pattern gains are cost-free and shrink live, so these are untested here, not disproved.

not_supported.name: Margin trend, free-cash-flow rank, buyback rank, Piotroski score, CAN SLIM, DCF, PEG, EPS growth, estimate revisions
not_supported.why: Each needs judgment, estimates data or untested cutoffs (S-029.P05, S-024.P03), or repeats the quality gate. No fundamentals data is approved.

not_supported.name: The valuation dial as a rule
not_supported.why: Described in the library as predictive over decades (S-031.P01, a single author's finding) but it never changes a trade, and a quarterly number invites overrides. At most context at the yearly review.

not_supported.name: Walk-forward parameter selection
not_supported.why: With only a few counted configs there is nothing to select. Settings stay fixed from the library, which saves tries.

not_supported.name: Tax-loss harvesting, currency hedging or timing, trading on the AI brain's picks
not_supported.why: Tax and currency depend on an unconfirmed regime (open questions on tax and currency), and timing or hedging them would be another untested rule. S-017.P03 only says conversion inside a foreign-index fund is a hidden cost to ask about; it says nothing on timing. The brain has no forward record and never moves money.

not_supported.name: Borrowing, options, short selling
not_supported.why: House rule: never. They can force a sale at the worst time, and nothing in the engine models them.

not_supported.name: Selling the index fund in a crash, or pausing the monthly purchase
not_supported.why: Pre-committed in the drawdown playbook. No test is registered that could override it (S-050.P01).

not_supported.name: A larger pot to chase +20% a year
not_supported.why: The goal is never a sizing input. Rules are judged against random baskets and the core, not against the goal.

not_supported.name: Checks the engine does not compute yet
not_supported.why: Plateau neighbours, review-day offsets, stale-signal placebo, leave-one-name-out, Reality Check, deflated Sharpe, paired, conditional and sector-matched nulls, regime or crash caps, hindsight-adjusted growth, per-period stability tests, the household account wrapper and the tries ledger. They are pre-registered requirements; none is checked today.

not_supported.name: Fundamental screens (quality gate, sales-per-share floor, combine ladder)
not_supported.why: Dormant (needs_data). No fundamentals data exists in the repo and no provider is approved. Nothing in them is tested.

not_supported.name: Corporate actions on held names (acquisition, delisting, bankruptcy, spin-off, reverse split, halt)
not_supported.why: No rule yet and the engine does not model them. Handled by hand with a dated note until the rule-change protocol adds one. A held name that stops trading is a missing-data case: the ledger keeps its last good track.

not_supported.name: The AI brain vetoing, adding or resizing a rule's order
not_supported.why: Never. The brain may explain and annotate; it has no forward record and nothing it says counts as a falsifier. An override would be a discretionary deviation under the pre-commitment.

not_supported.name: A rule for who may be added to the watchlist
not_supported.why: The 21 names were hand-picked with hindsight. An objective admission rule (for example top names by size per sector at a fixed date) cannot be tested without survivorship-free data. Until then any addition is a rule change: the engine has no add dates, so a new name is pickable after 253 days of prices, and a new freeze and ledger record are needed.

open_questions.question: Fundamentals data provider (none chosen): SEC filings (free, from about 2009, our own mapping), the current price vendor's add-on, a paid point-in-time database, or by-hand checks for held names only. Licence and public-repo limits must be checked for each. Which, if any?

Longer and survivorship-free history: approve a source for delisted prices and past index members, and a longer T-bill series (cash earns zero before the T-bill fund existed), or accept that satellite evidence rests on the forward record and a hindsight-biased decade?

Tax: country of residence, account types (can the pot sit in a tax-advantaged account?), tax on selling or on gains each year, holding-period rates, loss offsets, lot matching. Needed to price exits and turnover. Kept out of the public repo.

Currency: home currency, whether the broker holds a USD balance or converts every trade, the conversion fee, and whether the core should be a home-currency, hedged or accumulating fund (that price series would need a provider decision).
Broker facts: commission per order and minimum, order types, standing automatic orders, fractional shares. They set the cadence break-even check in E01 and any real-cost re-run.

Stock pot size and funding: the library says speculative money should be a few percent (S-020.P04), and the house proposes at most 10% of investable savings, funded once from new money, a windfall or a one-time sale of core units, or the 90/10 split of every payment, or 0% (Index Only). Which? Can both adults watch one slot fall by half without selling?
Backtests reset weights to equal each month; the household practice lets winners drift. Build the drift arm (E04) before any money?

Decided for this version: 182 days (half a year) of paper record before any money, as in docs/household.md; the research wanted 365. A longer wait can be chosen at the yearly review. Do we accept 182 days?

Decided for this version: the stock pot may replace at most 200% of itself a year (a sale and a purchase count once; rule v1 is about 210%). Fixed now; a change is a new freeze and a counted try. Do we accept it, or choose a lower ceiling such as 100% before the first real-data run?

Two choices kept outside tests: is the 8% 'never chase' stretch veto kept whatever a test shows, and does the pause-savings-when-the-core-is-weak gate stay out (registry default) or get registered at the next annual review?

Review cadence: the registry tests monthly Five Leaders with a quarterly arm (E05), and the forward ledger already records both. If quarterly wins by the E05 rule, follow its record beside the monthly one and leave the monthly record untouched?

House rule 3 (no entries near earnings or big macro events): keep it (live practice then differs from the tests, and skipped entries are logged), or turn it into a note-only step through the change protocol?

Is there a windfall (cash beyond the emergency reserve)? Lump sum (default) or staged over a fixed number of months, in writing now? How big is the emergency reserve (private)? Who places orders and who checks them?

Core allocation: no rule here sets an age-based bond or T-bill share or picks the core fund. Is the core 100% equity apart from the emergency reserve, or should a bond share with a 5-point drift band be registered (S-020.P04, S-022.P04)?

Benchmark: ranking by 12-1 return is the same against any benchmark, so it does not matter for the new rules; v1 still measures strength against QQQ. Re-point v1 to the core? That would be a v2 with a new record.

Freeze the 21-name watchlist and its sector labels? The program has no add dates: any addition or removal is a rule change under the protocol, a new freeze and a new forward record, and needs tries_counted raised. Do we accept that?
Financials and Utilities names (CME, AEP, XEL) are ineligible for the fundamental rungs. Accept that, or keep a separate price-only slot for them?

Before any planned check is built or its result read: freeze its method constants (Reality Check blocks of 3, 6 and 12 months, the drawdown-episode definition, Bartlett lag 12, seed 20261005), and pass the second-source price check (docs/decisions.md) before any correlation claim or before dropping v1's correlation cap.

House rules versus this registry: docs/household.md rule 2 (3 of 4 setup checks), rule 4 (a name leaves when the rule drops it; no averaging down by default) and the trust ladder describe rule v1. If Five Leaders is ever adopted they must be rewritten with a change note first. Until then the house rules stay as they are. Agreed?
